summary: Specifies the Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol, which lets provider edge devices in a redundancy group synchronize data to provide redundancy for VPWS and VPLS services. It supports both attachment circuit and pseudowire redundancy.

eli5.summary: Two routers work as a team so if one breaks the other takes over. They use this protocol to keep talking and sharing what they know.

questions: what is a redundancy group in l2vpn
how does iccp detect pe failure
subtitle: A protocol, carried inside LDP, that lets redundant provider edge routers share state so a backup can take over for a failed one.

tldr.problem: Layer 2 VPN services want provider edge (PE) routers to back each other up, but the routers in a redundancy group must coordinate which one is active and share configuration and state.
tldr.mechanism: ICCP runs as a secondary protocol inside LDP sessions between the PEs of a Redundancy Group. It manages membership and application connections, and carries application data for pseudowire redundancy and multi-chassis LACP.
tldr.outcome: Client applications get reliable, in-order state synchronization, and PE failure is detected with existing mechanisms such as BFD. ICCP is meant for well-managed networks, not the public Internet.

today: RFC 7275 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2014. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why PEs Need to Talk: Redundancy Groups
sections.content:
Network availability matters to service providers because outages cost revenue and can bring penalties under Service Level Agreements. This document defines the Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol (ICCP), which synchronizes state and configuration between two or more PE nodes that form a Redundancy Group (RG). Here a chassis is simply an L2VPN PE node. The protocol supports multi-chassis redundancy on either attachment circuits (ACs) or pseudowires (PWs), for both VPWS and VPLS services.

RG members fall under a single administration and offer multi-homed connectivity to a device (such as a CE) or a whole access network. The redundancy mechanism toward access could be IEEE 802.1AX link aggregation with LACP or SONET APS; its details are out of scope, but the PEs must exchange state for it to work. With an inter-chassis channel, PEs can also elect which pseudowires are active or standby and tell the remote end the result.

ICCP is built as a secondary protocol inside LDP, reusing LDP sessions, the TCP transport and TCP-based security that PEs already need for pseudowires.

The RFC lists four ways to link the PEs for ICCP: co-located or geo-redundant, each with a dedicated interconnect or a shared one through the core network. A dedicated link can rely on Layer 2 resilience such as link aggregation; a shared path can use PSN mechanisms such as RSVP LSPs with Fast Reroute.
sections.eli5: Two routers work as a team so a customer stays connected even if one breaks. ICCP is how the two teammates talk.

sections.title: What ICCP Has to Provide
sections.content:
The RFC lists requirements the protocol must meet.

  • A control channel (not data traffic) between RG members, with low bandwidth, low delay and high reliability.
  • Support for multiple client applications, so messages are extensible (TLV-based) with registration and versioning.
  • Reliable, in-order transport with authentication, since lost or reordered messages would harm the applications.
  • A way to monitor PE health that detects node failure, ideally sub-second (about 50 to 150 msec).
  • Event-driven updates rather than timer-based ones.
  • Multi-link and multi-hop interconnects.
  • Transport security: ICCP MUST NOT accept connections from arbitrary devices and must prevent source address spoofing.
  • Static configuration of RG members. Two nodes cover most deployments, but more are not precluded, and one node can be in several RGs.

ICCP is modeled in three layers: an Application layer for the redundancy applications, an Inter-Chassis Communication (ICC) layer for versioning, membership and connections, and a Transport layer for delivery and failure detection.
sections.eli5: The notes between the helpers must arrive, arrive in order, and come only from the real teammate, not from a stranger.

sections.title: Joining a Group and Connecting Applications
sections.content:
When an RG is enabled on a PE, an LDP session to every remote PE in the RG MUST exist, and the ICCP capability is advertised using RFC 5561 capability messages. The PE then sends an RG Connect message. The ICCP connection for an RG is operational only when both sides have sent and received RG Connect. A PE MUST reject a connect if it is not a member of that RG or if its connection limit is exceeded. RG Disconnect tears the connection down unilaterally, with no acknowledgement.

Each ICCP connection has a state machine with six states: NONEXISTENT, INITIALIZED, CAPSENT, CAPREC, CONNECTING and OPERATIONAL. Each client application then gets its own Application Connection, brought up by an Application Connect TLV carried in RG Connect, with its own six-state machine (NONEXISTENT, RESET, CONNSENT, CONNREC, CONNECTING, OPERATIONAL). An ICCP connection must be operational first.

Applications negotiate a version. A higher version in a Connect TLV is rejected with an Incompatible Protocol Version NAK; a lower one MAY be accepted at that version or rejected; an equal one is honored or rejected by configuration and connection count.

Protected links, ports and PWs are called Redundant Objects, each identified by a 64-bit opaque Redundant Object ID (ROID) that MUST match across RG members. An optional separate LDP session (using a non-zero label space identifier) can carry ICCP when a lot of data must be exchanged quickly.
sections.eli5: First the two helpers say hello and agree they are on the same team. Then each job they share gets its own agreement.

sections.title: ICCP Messages
sections.content:
ICCP reuses LDP infrastructure with a new set of LDP message types in the range 0x0700 to 0x070F. Every message starts with an ICC header: U-bit, Message Type, Message Length, a 4-octet Message ID, and an ICC RG ID TLV (type 0x0005, length 4), followed by mandatory and optional parameters. RG ID 0 is reserved.

Four messages are defined: RG Connect (0x0700), RG Disconnect (0x0701), RG Notification (0x0702) and RG Application Data (0x0703). Connect carries an ICC Sender Name TLV, the sender's host name in UTF-8 and at most 80 octets, plus zero or one Application Connect TLV. Disconnect carries a status code, either ICCP RG Removed or ICCP Application Removed from RG. Notification rejects a connection, an application connection, a message or some TLVs, using a NAK TLV with a status code and the rejected Message ID. Application Data carries TLVs for exactly one application.

The ICCP capability TLV used in LDP capability negotiation has code point 0x0700, and this document specifies version 1.0.
sections.eli5: There are only a few kinds of notes: hello, goodbye, I-cannot-do-that, and the notes with actual news.

sections.title: Pseudowire Redundancy Application
sections.content:
The PW-RED application lets the PEs in an RG agree which pseudowire forwards. It SHOULD NOT run together with an AC redundancy application on the same service instance, to avoid deadlock between the two mechanisms.

After the application connection is up, each PE advertises its PW configuration (PW-RED Config TLV) including the ROID, the redundancy mode, a priority, a service name and the PW identifier. The mode is Master, Slave, Independent, or Independent with Request Switchover. If a received mode does not match the local mode for the same ROID, the PE MUST reject it, disable the local pseudowire and SHOULD raise an alarm, so misconfiguration cannot create forwarding loops.

PEs then exchange PW status. In Independent Mode, the PE with the best (numerically least) PW Priority advertises active Preferential Forwarding status on its pseudowires and the others advertise standby. In Master/Slave Mode the Master side picks a single active pseudowire. A PE can ask a peer to resend state with a synchronization request, answered between start and end Synchronization Data TLVs.

When a PE sees that a remote RG member is unreachable, and it has the highest priority after the failed PE, it becomes active and activates its pseudowires.
sections.eli5: The helpers pick who does the work now and who waits. If the worker disappears, the next one in line steps up.

sections.title: Attachment Circuit Redundancy and mLACP
sections.content:
For redundancy on attachment circuits, an AC redundancy application tells the other PEs by ICCP Application Data messages when an AC fails or the PE is isolated from the core, so a standby PE can take over. If AC redundancy runs over ICCP, then Independent Mode of PW redundancy (RFC 6870) MUST be used, and each PW's active or standby status is derived from the ACs. For VPWS, with one AC per service, the PW follows the AC. For VPLS, the PW is active if at least one AC is active, and standby only when all ACs are standby.

The multi-chassis LACP (mLACP) application serves Ethernet ACs. PEs exchange system, Aggregator and port configuration first, then Aggregator and port state, and the PEs MUST agree on System ID, System Priority and the Aggregator MAC address by using the values from the PE with the numerically lowest System Aggregation Priority. Duplicate Node IDs are rejected.

On failure, a PE hit by a core isolation fault by default brings down its links toward the CE so the CE fails over to the other PE. After recovery, a PE with revertive protection MAY reclaim the active role by sending an mLACP Port Priority TLV.
sections.eli5: The customer's cable plugs into both routers. If one router is cut off, it unplugs itself so the customer uses the other one.

sections.title: Detecting a Failed PE
sections.content:
ICCP tells its client applications when a remote RG member is no longer reachable, so they can start failover. It does not define its own keep-alive. It reuses existing detection: a Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (RFC 5880) session between the PEs, or monitoring of IP reachability through IGP or BGP. Both assume connectivity to the remote PE is itself protected, so a loss means the node failed. On a shared interconnect the signal means the PE failed or was isolated from the MPLS network.

The RFC warns that loss of the LDP session is not a reliable sign that the remote PE is down, because the session can reset while the PE keeps forwarding traffic.
sections.eli5: Instead of building a new alarm, the helpers use the alarms they already have to notice when the other one has stopped.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
ICCP SHOULD only be used in well-managed, highly monitored networks, and ought not be deployed on or over the public Internet. It is not intended for an RG that spans different administrative domains.

Implementations MUST let the operator choose which LDP peers get the ICCP capability and which are accepted, and an incoming ICCP connection MUST NOT be accepted unless its source address belongs to an eligible peer. The TCP Authentication Option (RFC 5925) SHOULD be used, and the LDP MD5 option MAY be used for backward compatibility. The MPLS security framework (RFC 5920) also applies.

Activity on attachment circuits can be abused for denial of service, for example a malicious CE sending constantly changing LACP messages or link bouncing, leading to many ICCP exchanges. Implementations SHOULD offer control-plane policing.
sections.eli5: Only trusted teammates may join the conversation, and nobody should be able to flood the helpers with fake notes.

items.label: RG Connect
items.desc: Declares RG membership and can open an application connection.

items.label: RG Disconnect
items.desc: Leaves the RG or closes one application connection.

items.label: RG Notification
items.desc: Rejects a connection, message or TLVs using a NAK TLV.

items.label: RG Application Data
items.desc: Carries data for exactly one application.

layers.label: Application layer
layers.detail: Redundancy applications such as PW-RED and mLACP

layers.label: ICC layer
layers.detail: Versioning, RG membership, Redundant Object identification, connection management

layers.label: Transport layer
layers.detail: Addressing, flow control, reliable in-order delivery, failure detection
